content.title: Artemis II weather forecast: '80% go' for launch day
content.text: The forecast remains encouraging despite recent rain this week because of a very well understood cycle driven by the seabreeze. Posted 3/31/2026, 7:49:48 PM Updated 4/1/2026, 12:37:29 PM Video Player is loading.Current Time 0:00Duration 2:02Remaining Time 2:02 NASA preps for mission around the moon Four astronauts, including NC State graduate Christina Koch, are scheduled to launch for the moon on Wednesday, April 1. Weather conditions are looking favorable, and there is an 80% chance that the Artemis II mission is a "go." The window is 6:24 p.m. to 8:24 p.m. All eyes on the weather The launch will happen at NASA's Kennedy Space Center, and as of Wednesday morning, weather conditions in central Florida still look favorable. NASA is shooting for the moon. A guide to the Artemis II mission Florida is experiencing a well-understood pattern driven by the seabreeze effect. As the land warms up more quickly than the ocean, a steady breeze develops, pushing moisture from the Atlantic onto the coast. Moon rocket and weather are on NASA's side for the first astronaut launch in decades Clouds build throughout the morning, often leading to scattered showers and the occasional thunderstorm in the afternoon. By the evening, these storms typically migrate toward Tampa and the rest of the Gulf side of the state, leaving the Atlantic coast clearer. Forecasters aren't seeing this as a significant threat for Wednesday evening's launch but will be closely watching clouds to the west of the launch pad, particularly cumulus clouds -- the low-level, detached, puffy clouds with flat bases and distinct, cauliflower-like outlines. Trip to the moon: How meteorologists determine go/no-go for Wednesday's Artemis II launch attempt Cumulus clouds, in the early stages of their lifecycle, are an indication of fair weather, but they can mature into lightning generators that would violate launch weather criteria, postponing the launch at least to the next day. Or, they might be create temporary conditions that could pass, leaving sufficient time to launch during the two-hour launch window. Meet the crew Artemis astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen have been in quarantine preparing for the launch. The Artemis II mission means the moon is about to welcome its first woman, first person of color and first non-American. Koch already holds the record for the longest single spaceflight by a woman. During her 328-day mission at the International Space Station spanning 2019 and 2020, she took part in the first all-female spacewalk. Glover, a Navy test pilot, was the first Black astronaut to live and work aboard the space station in 2020 and 2021. He also was one of the first astronauts to launch with SpaceX. The Canadian Space Agency’s Hansen, a former fighter pilot, is the lone space rookie. Their commander is Wiseman, a retired Navy captain who lived aboard the space station in 2014 and later headed NASA’s astronaut corps. They range in age from 47 to 50. Watch parties in the Triangle Several venues are hosting watch parties for the launch. Talley Student Union at NC State will stream the Artemis II launch between 5:30 p.m. and 7:45 p.m. on the Pavillion TV (located on the ground level near Talley Market). All are invited. A watch event at the North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences is already full. © 2026 Copyright Capitol Broadcasting Company
